Conjugacy classes in \(A_7\) are obtained from even cycle types in \(S_7\), with the rule that an \(S_7\)-class splits in \(A_7\) only if the cycle type has all distinct odd parts. For partitions of \(7\), the only such even type is \(7\), so the 7-cycles split into two \(A_7\)-classes.

The even cycle types in \(A_7\) are:

\[
\begin{aligned}
1^7 &: \mathrm{id},\\
2^2 1^3 &: (12)(34),\\
3 1^4 &: (123),\\
3^2 1 &: (123)(456),\\
3 2^2 &: (123)(45)(67),\\
4 2 1 &: (1234)(56),\\
5 1^2 &: (12345),\\
7 &: \text{two classes}.
\end{aligned}
\]

That gives \(7\) single classes plus \(2\) classes from the split 7-cycle class, for a total of \(9\).

Your list contains all except the class of type \(3+2+2\). Therefore the missing conjugacy class is represented by

\[
\boxed{(123)(45)(67)}.
\]
